summary: Layer 1B expansion for the optical-glass/IR-optics chokepoint finds one unusually direct small-cap discovery candidate, two mid/large-cap underfollowed component/materials candidates, and one larger reference/customer-anchor. The strongest policy evidence is FY2026 NDAA Section 834, which directs DoD to develop and implement a strategy to eliminate reliance on covered nations for optical glass or optical systems by January 1, 2030. The strongest company-specific exposure found in this pass is LightPath Technologies, where public disclosures tie germanium-free infrared optics to an F-35-related order. Materion and MKS are plausible second-order suppliers because they provide precision optics, coatings, photonics components, and optical assemblies to defense or defense-adjacent markets, but their exact revenue sensitivity to the NDAA optical-glass mandate needs verification. Teledyne is included as a reference demand anchor through Teledyne FLIR, not as an obscure supplier.
